rows.definition: Something published for others to meet. Also an upright that bears weight, and to send onward.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Something published for others to come across, an upright that bears weight, or the act of sending a thing onward — three senses sharing one image of something fixed in place.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin postis (an upright, doorpost), and separately positus (placed), both related to ponere (to place); a thing published for others to meet, an upright that bears weight, and the act of sending onward all share one root in something fixed or set in place.

rows.definition: What a thing could become but has not. Potential is real and is not yet evidence of anything.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A capacity credited to a thing before it has done anything to earn the credit — real, and never mistaken here for a result already delivered.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin potentia (power, capability), from potens (powerful), from posse (to be able); what a thing has the power to become but has not yet, real without yet being evidence of anything.

rows.definition: The Windows shell of objects and verbs — half the street wakes here; its quirks are documented so they bite once.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The command-line environment of objects and verbs that half the house's own street wakes into, with its quirks documented so they only bite once.
rows.historical_meaning: From power (Old French poeir, to be able) and shell (Old English sciell, a hard covering, extended in 1960s computing to a command interpreter); Microsoft's 2006 name for its object-and-verb scripting environment.

rows.definition: Concerned with what actually works rather than what should. Of judgment tested against use.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Concerned with what actually works when it is tried, rather than with what ought to work in principle.
rows.historical_meaning: Greek πρακτικός (praktikos, fit for action), from πράσσειν (prassein, to do, achieve); judgment concerned with what actually works when tested against use, rather than what should work in principle.

rows.definition: Repeated doing that builds capacity. Also the settled way a group works — both mean something done often enough to become known.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Capacity built by doing a thing again and again until it takes less thought each time. Also the way work actually gets carried out here, which is not always the way it is written down to be carried out.
rows.historical_meaning: Greek πρακτική (praktikē, practical [skill]), from πράσσειν (prassein, to do, perform); repeated doing until it becomes settled and known, whether by a single hand or a whole group.

rows.definition: Before. A part placed at the front to move a thing earlier in time or order.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Before. A part set at the front of a word to move the whole of it earlier in time or in order.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin prae (before, in front of), from Proto-Indo-European *per- (forward, in front); a part placed at the front to move a thing earlier in time or order.

rows.definition: What is said before the substance, to set what follows in place. A preamble is orientation, not content.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: What is said before the substance, walking ahead of it to set the ground the rest will stand on. It orients; it is not itself content.
rows.historical_meaning: Medieval Latin praeambulum (a walking before), from prae- (before) + ambulare (to walk); what is said before the substance, walking ahead of it to set the ground it will stand on.

rows.definition: The first stage that raises a weak signal enough to be worked with. Everything after it inherits what it did.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The first stage that raises a weak signal enough to be worked with. Everything that follows inherits whatever this stage did to it.
rows.historical_meaning: From pre- (Latin prae, before) and amplify (Latin amplificare, to make larger, from amplus, large, + facere, to make); the first stage that raises a weak signal before every stage that follows inherits what it did.

rows.definition: Made in advance rather than on demand. Prebuilding trades flexibility for speed at the moment of use.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Made in advance rather than on demand, trading the flexibility of building fresh for the speed of already having it ready.
rows.historical_meaning: From pre- (Latin prae, before) and build (Old English byldan, to construct); made in advance of the moment it is needed, trading flexibility for speed at the point of use.

rows.definition: How finely a value is stated. Distinct from accuracy — a precise number can be precisely wrong.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: How finely a value is stated, which is not the same as accuracy — a precise number can still be precisely wrong.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin praecisio (a cutting off short), from praecidere (to cut off in front), from prae- (before) + caedere (to cut); a value stated exactly, cut cleanly rather than left rough — and distinct from accuracy, since a precise cut can still miss its mark.

rows.definition: Short form of preference. A leaning toward one option, held without needing justification.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Short for preference — a leaning toward one option, held without needing to be argued for.
rows.historical_meaning: A shortening of preference, from Latin praeferre (to bear before, prefer), from prae- (before) + ferre (to carry); a leaning toward one option, held without needing to be argued for.

rows.definition: A leaning toward one option over another, held without needing justification. A preference is stated, not argued.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: What a person reaches for when nothing forces the choice, kept as a fact about them rather than a position to defend. The house follows a stated preference and asks for no reason behind it.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin praeferre (to carry before, prefer), from prae- (before) + ferre (to carry); a leaning toward one option, carried ahead of the others without needing justification.

rows.definition: Leans toward one option over another. In interfaces, the stated setting a body needs rather than wants.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Leans toward one option over another — in an interface, the setting a body actually needs rather than merely wants.
rows.historical_meaning: From Latin praeferre (to carry before, prefer), from prae- (before) + ferre (to carry); leaning toward one option over another, carried ahead of the rest.

rows.definition: A part placed before a word to change its meaning. It carries no meaning alone and alters everything it joins.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A part placed before a word to change its meaning. It carries none of its own, and alters everything it is attached to.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin praefigere (to fasten in front), from prae- (before) + figere (to fix, fasten); a part fastened before a word that carries no meaning alone and changes everything it joins.

rows.definition: To fetch a thing before it is asked for. Preloading spends effort on a guess about what will be wanted.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To fetch a thing before it has been asked for, spending effort now on a guess about what will be wanted later.
rows.historical_meaning: From pre- (Latin prae, before) and load (Old English hlæstan, to put a burden aboard); to fetch a thing before it is asked for, spending effort now on a guess about what will be wanted.

rows.definition: Above the standard offering, at a higher price. Premium is a claim about tier, not about quality.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Above the standard offering, and priced accordingly. Premium is a claim about tier, and never, by itself, a claim about quality.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin praemium (a reward, a share taken before the rest), from prae- (before) + emere (to take, buy); a claim about tier and priority, not about quality — the portion set aside ahead of the ordinary share.

rows.definition: That which prepares material before the main work begins. It runs first so the real process can assume things.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: That which prepares material before the main work begins, running first so the process after it can safely assume what it has already done.
rows.historical_meaning: From pre- (Latin prae, before) and process (Latin procedere, to go forward), with the agent suffix -or; that which runs first so the main process that follows can assume what it has already done.

rows.definition: Being here, and being felt to be here. Presence is more than location — it is attention actually given.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Being here, and being felt to be here. Presence asks for more than location; it asks that attention was actually given.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin praesentia, from praesens (being at hand), from praeesse (to be in front, be at hand), from prae- (before) + esse (to be); being here in a way that is felt, not merely located.

rows.definition: The keeping of a thing against loss and decay. Preservation is active work, not storage.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The active keeping of a thing against loss and decay — work that has to continue, not storage that can simply sit.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin praeservare (to guard in advance), from prae- (before) + servare (to keep, watch over); the active, ongoing keeping of a thing against loss, done ahead of the loss rather than after it.

rows.definition: To keep from loss or change — protection across time; lose-nothing made a verb.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To keep a thing from loss or change across time — the house's own law of losing nothing, turned into a single verb.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin praeservare (to guard beforehand), from prae- (before) + servare (to keep, watch over); to keep a thing from loss or change across time, protection made a verb.

rows.definition: That which keeps a thing against loss and decay. Preservation is active work, not storage.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: That which does the ongoing work of keeping a thing safe from loss and decay, rather than merely holding it in place.
rows.historical_meaning: From Latin praeservare (to guard beforehand), from prae- (before) + servare (to keep); that which does the active, ongoing work of keeping a thing against loss and decay.

rows.definition: A saved arrangement of settings, ready to be chosen whole. Someone's earlier good decision, offered again.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A saved arrangement of settings, ready to be chosen as a whole — someone's earlier good decision, offered again to whoever needs it next.
rows.historical_meaning: From pre- (Latin prae, before) and set (Old English settan, to place); an earlier good decision about settings, arranged in advance and offered again whole.

rows.definition: To push with steady force. Also the making public of what was written — both apply pressure until something takes.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To push with a steady force, or to make something public by printing it — both apply pressure until an impression finally takes.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin premere (to press, push), via the frequentative pressare; a steady applied force, and — by way of the printing press that stamps an impression under it — the making public of what was written.

rows.definition: To reformat a thing so it reads better. Prettifying changes presentation and must not change content.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To reformat a thing so it is easier to read, changing only how it presents and never, if it is done honestly, what it actually says.
rows.historical_meaning: From Old English prættig (cunning, skillful, later attractive) with -ify (Latin -ficare, to make); to reformat a thing so it reads better, changing only how it looks and never what it says.

rows.definition: Short form of previous. The one coming before this in an order.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Short for previous — the one that comes before this one in an order.
rows.historical_meaning: A shortening of previous, from Latin praevius (going before), from prae- (before) + via (way); the one coming before this in an order.

rows.definition: A showing of what a thing will be before it is committed. A preview reduces surprise at the cost of finality.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A showing of what a thing will be, offered before it is finally committed to, which reduces surprise at the price of not yet being final.
rows.historical_meaning: From pre- (Latin prae, before) and view (Old French vue, from Latin vidēre, to see); a 20th-century cinema term for a showing of what a thing will be before it is finally committed.

rows.definition: Coming before this one. Previousness is a fact about order, and carries no claim about being superseded.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Coming before this one in an order, which is a fact about sequence alone and carries no claim about being superseded.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin praevius (going before), from prae- (before) + via (way, road); coming before this one in order, without any claim about being superseded.
